body.statement: \(\textsc{Explicit-Max-Tail}\), whose encoded instance consists of \(a\), a rational \(\delta\), every labeled rational coordinate \(y_i^{\mathrm{obs},\delta}\) with \(i\notin M(a)\), the support \(\Omega\) listed row by row, every rational weight \(w_z\), and a rational threshold \(q\), is NP-complete. Membership in NP is certified by a complete weak order together with a rational representative \(b\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\) of polynomial encoding length; a polynomial-time verifier checks the observed-coordinate equalities, the represented weak order and midranks, and the exact rational weighted tail inequality \(p(a,b)\ge q\). NP-hardness holds for instances \(\mathsf R(G,s)\) with \(v\) missing realized-treated outcomes, four realized controls, two distinct observed outcome values, \(n=3v-s+4\) units, and \(1+2v+|E|\) explicitly listed rows with polynomial-bit rational weights. A completion reaches \(q_\star\) if and only if its \(s\) lowest tied missing labels induce an \(s\)-clique in \(G\).
body.justification: The result shows that the chamber explosion reflects intrinsic completion difficulty rather than a naive implementation.
body.gap: The exact-test literature reports combinatorial cost but supplies no decision-complexity classification for a rationally weighted explicit support with missing midranks.
body.consumer: Software can justify exact fixed-\(k\) computation and principled approximation when attrition is large.
